stories.title: Immune and microbial responses associated with extreme climatic conditions in the vermetid Dendropoma cristatum
stories.description: Extreme climatic events are increasingly recognized as major drivers of rapid ecological change in coastal marine ecosystems, with particularly severe consequences for habitat-forming intertidal species. In the Mediterranean basin, vermetid reefs represent ecologically relevant yet still neglected bioconstructions that contribute to shoreline complexity, biodiversity maintenance, and ecosystem functioning. Here, we investigated physiological and microbial responses of the reef-builder Dendropoma cristatum following an extreme desiccation event, recorded along the northern coast of Sicily during summer 2022. Specimens were collected from two contrasting reef portions: the outer edge, directly exposed to prolonged emersion, and the permanently submerged cuvette, used as a control condition. Across three Sicilian coastal areas, we assessed immune-related enzymatic activities—glutathione peroxidase (GPx), phenoloxidase (PO), and lysozyme (LYS)—together with the composition of associated microbial communities through 16S rRNA gene sequencing. GPx and PO activities were consistently and significantly higher in outer edge specimens, indicating activation of antioxidant and immune-related defenses under stressful conditions, whereas LYS activity showed no significant differences. Bacterial community structure also differed between reef zones, with outer edge gastropod showing shifts in the relative abundance of several taxa, including Vibrionaceae and Rhodobacteraceae. Overall, our findings suggest that extreme environmental futures could rapidly affect D. cristatum at both physiological and microbial levels, providing new insight into the vulnerability of Mediterranean vermetid reefs to ongoing climate change.

stories.title: An integrated methodology and sensitivity analysis for the prediction and multiobjective optimization of the thermophysical properties of MWCNT/water nanofluids using SVR-GA and SPEA2
stories.description: This study proposes an integrated methodology that utilizes intelligent computing to precisely predict and optimize the thermophysical properties of a three-dimensional multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)/water nanofluid. Two distinct Support Vector Regression (SVR) models, enhanced by hyperparameter optimization using a Genetic Algorithm (GA), were successfully trained to accurately estimate the dynamic viscosity (DV) and thermal conductivity (TC) based on experimental data across a range of volume concentrations (0–0.5%) and temperatures (30–65 °C). The resulting SVR-GA models demonstrated high predictive accuracy, evidenced by the test data’s mean and maximum relative percentage errors: 0.4546% and 0.9690% for DV, and 0.5950% and 0.9532% for TC, respectively. Moreover, the trained SVR models have been validated using K-fold cross-validation, and the network’s accuracy in estimating unseen data has been demonstrated. A sensitivity analysis confirmed that temperature exerts a greater influence on nanofluid properties than volume concentration. Leveraging these high-accuracy models, a multiobjective optimization problem was formulated to simultaneously minimize DV and maximize TC. This problem was solved using the Strength Pareto Evolutionary Algorithm 2 (SPEA2), which yielded a Pareto front of optimal trade-off solutions. The analysis of the Pareto front consistently identified 65 °C as the optimal operating temperature, providing useful insights for selecting conditions that maximize the nanofluid’s heat transfer efficiency.

stories.title: Operational risk assessment of distribution networks considering electric vehicle V2G strategies
stories.description: Large-scale EV integration changes both when and where load appears in distribution networks, which makes nodal voltage and branch power flow more vulnerable to concentrated demand. This study develops an operational risk assessment framework for distribution networks under EV V2G strategies. An EV spatiotemporal charging/discharging model is first built from trip-chain behavior and dynamic state-of-charge evolution, and two V2G modes are then described: a fixed-schedule strategy and a risk-guided strategy. On that basis, a probabilistic power flow model is established to capture the uncertainty of distributed generation, conventional demand, and EV behavior. Weighted distribution entropy is employed to represent explicit risks associated with voltage and branch-flow limit violations, while Theil entropy is introduced to measure the unevenness of state-variable changes, and the two are combined into a comprehensive risk index. Simulations on a modified IEEE 33-bus system under three operating scenarios show that the proposed method can clearly track how operational risk evolves over time under different V2G strategies. Among the compared cases, the risk-guided V2G strategy provides the most effective peak-risk suppression and delivers a smoother risk profile during critical periods.
